abstract: Maintains nearshore approach bathymetry assessments, shallow-water landing permits, and shallow-water trenching progress rates
system_message:
You are Coastal hydrographic lead (COAST). The Coastal hydrographic lead (COAST) maintains records covering nearshore approach bathymetry assessments, shallow-water landing permits, and shallow-water trenching progress rates, alongside tidal current monitoring observations for seabed trenching spreads.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains nearshore approach bathymetry assessments, shallow-water landing permits, and shallow-water trenching progress rates（HYDRO）
information_points.content:
COAST-HYDRO-E06：For the Celtic Horizon Ploughtrench Fleet, nearshore landing environmental authorization is not approved within the shore landing corridor in territorial waters, and its nearshore trenching rate across the intertidal approach is 80 m/h.
COAST-HYDRO-JQI：For the North Sea Mechanical Trenching Spread, nearshore landing environmental authorization is approved within the shore landing corridor in territorial waters, and its nearshore trenching rate across the intertidal approach is 60 m/h.
COAST-HYDRO-7FK：For the Baltic Subsea Jetting Fleet, nearshore landing environmental authorization is approved within the shore landing corridor in territorial waters, and its nearshore trenching rate across the intertidal approach is 40 m/h.

information_points.title: Tidal current monitoring（TIDE）
information_points.content:
COAST-TIDE-0TL：For the Baltic Subsea Jetting Fleet, the maximum allowable spring tide velocity permitting diverless trenching sled alignment in the intertidal landfall zone is 2.1 kn.
COAST-TIDE-GXO：For the North Sea Mechanical Trenching Spread, the maximum allowable spring tide velocity permitting diverless trenching sled alignment in the intertidal landfall zone is 2.8 kn.
COAST-TIDE-9T6：For the Celtic Horizon Ploughtrench Fleet, the maximum allowable spring tide velocity permitting diverless trenching sled alignment in the intertidal landfall zone is 3.5 kn.
